rows.author: C060
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED FOUR HUNDRED NINETY-THREE, ENTITLED: "AN ACT TO PROHIBIT THE USE OR CONFERRING OF MILITARY OR NAVAL GRADES OR TITLES BY OR UPON PERSONS NOT IN THE SERVICE OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES OR THE PHILIPPINE CONSTABULARY, TO REGULATE THE WEARING, USE, MANUFACTURE AND SALE OF INSIGNIAS, DECORATIONS AND MEDALS, BADGES, PATCHES AND IDENTIFICATION CARDS PRESCRIBED FOR THE SAID ARMED FORCES OR CONSTABULARY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES"
rows.abstract: The proposed bill seeks to STOP the practice of use or conferring of military, naval or police grades or titles by or upon persons not in the service of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police. Instead of merely regulating the wearing use, manufacture and sale of insignias, decorations and medals, badges, patches and identification cards prescribed for the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Philippine National Police, the bill COMPLETELY PROHIBITS the possession and use of said items by unauthorized personnel.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2003-01-21

rows.author: C019
rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTRICTING THE USE OF GOVERNMENT VEHICLES TO OFFICIAL USE, PROVIDING CERTAIN EXEMPTIONS AND PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Government Vehicle Utilization Act of 2993." This bill prohibits (1) the use of government office vehicles for security back up provided for designated government officials; (2) use of government vehicles for personal purposes; (3) repairs, maintenance or fuel allocation for vehicles assigned to any public officials or employees used by them for purposes other than official and authorized; and (4) reimbursement of costs or allocation if the vehicles used do not bear the appropriate markings, appropriate license plates, and are not currently registered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2003-01-22

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE WELFARE OF THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD BY INCREASING, INTEGRATING AND RATIONALIZING THE BASE PAY AND OTHER BENEFITS OF ITS OFFICERS AND ENLISTED PERSONNEL, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Magna Carta of the Philippine Coast Guard." It is the objective of this Act to ensure reforms in the organization of the Philippine Coast Guard by bestowing to every personnel the enjoyment of basic rights and privileges in his career in the Coast Guard service and upon retirement. As provided for in this bill, the State shall: (a) Promote and maintain a rationalized and professional Coast Guard service; (b) Facilitate administrative and financial support to every PCG personnel and/or hisfamily facing criminal or civil suit arising from service-related "acts of omissions" and in the course of his duty; (c) Promote and develop a rational system of career promotion and advancement based on merit and a uniform criteria, applicable to evvery PCG personnel; (d) Develop every Coast Guard personnel to be highly competent and professional by institutionaliz ing the PCG as a strong cohesive and well-balanced bureau of government; and (e) Assure the rights of every PCG personnel to securi
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2003-01-22

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 109, CHAPTER I, TITLE IV OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1158, AS AMENDED, UP TO REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8424, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPPOSES THEREOF(RE: VAT ON FILM INDUSTRY)
rows.abstract: Rationale: The imposition of ten percent (10%) Value-added Tax (VAT) increases the amount of tax paid by the members of the film industry to a grant total of thirty percent (30%) of their income. It runs contrary to the policy of the State to support and develop the local film industry. The imposition of 10% VAT is another disincentive to the film industry to produce films of superior quality and to enhance the skills and talents of Filipino artists anf fil, producers. To precent the dying filmindustry from going down further and to promote the development and growth of the local film industry, this bill seeks to exempt the members of the film industry and the other individuals in the same category from the imposition of the 10% Value-addded Tax.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2003-01-27

rows.author: C011
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A CAP ON PUBLIC DEBT IN ORDER TO ENSURE LONG-TERM FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY THROUGH FISCAL DISCIPLINE
rows.abstract: "Debt Cap Act of 2003." This bill states that within five (5) years from the enactment of this proposed measure into law, the consolidated outstanding debt of the National government and of government-owne d and/or controlled corporations shall notexceed, at any one time, an amount equivalent to 100 percent of the country's nominal Gross Domestic Product and within another five years and thereafter, said outstanding debt shall not exceed 80 percent of the country's Gross Domestic Product: PROVIDED, That in no case within this second five year period will level of outstanding debt exceed 100 percent of Gross Domestic Product.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2003-01-27

rows.author: D045
rows.title_full: AN ACT CALLING FOR A CONSTITUTIONAL CONVENTION FOR THE EXPRESSED PURPOSE OF REVISING THE EXISTING 1987 CONSTITUTION, OR FORMULATING AMENDMENTS TO IT FOR THE APPROVAL OF THE ELECTORATE, PROVIDING FOR QUALIFIED REPRESENTATION PER LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTAND OTHER DETAILS PERTAINING TO THE HOLDING OF THE CONVENTION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFORE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Constitutional Convention Act of 2003." Rationale: The country is presently besieged with opinions from the public and private sectors, as well as from various agencies of the government, on the propriety of introducing amendments to, or rewritingor substantially changing the 1987 Constitution of the Philippines. It may be a coincidence however, that the fundamental law of our land has constantly and glaringly been attached with this proposal every time there is a nearing of a change in the administration. It is inevitable therefore that the public would counclude that a politically motivated conspiracy exists, and it is to this end that the author of this bill proposes a Constitutional Convention be assembled to put this matter to rest..> The Constitutional Convention proposed herein shall be composed of a delegate per legislative district in the country. They shall be duly qualified and voted simultaneous with the synchronized elections in 2004. The delegates to the Convention sha
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS since 2003-01-21

rows.abstract: "National Food Authority Reorganization Act of 2002." This bill seeks to strengthen the National Food Authority to ensure food security for all Filipinos and provide an orderly development to the foodgrains marketing industry so that it can extend sufficient motivations to farmers and producers to increase their productivity and competiteveness . To execute these objectives, the National food Corporation (NFC) is hereby created. > The management of the Corporation shall be vested in a Presidentwho shall be appointed by the President of the Philippines for three (3) years and who shall direct and manage the affairs of the Corporation. > This proposed measure also seeks to create the Food Development and Regulatory Administration (FDRA) whiich shall carry out regulatory as well as scientific and development functions for strengthening the efficiency of the food supply chain to increase the value of farmer's produce as a component of food products for export as well as against imports.

rows.abstract: This bill requires the President of the Philippines to obtain Congressional approval of the exact amount, rate of interest and actual source of all intended yearly borrowings in the name and liability of the Republic of the Philippines. The notification shall contain the probable terms and condtions, interest rates, maturity period, penalties in case of default or late payments of amortizations, and other similar conditions, and shall be transmitted yearly to Congress together with the proposedannual appropriations act.> Contracting of all forms of public debt in the name and liability of the Republic of the Philippines without the prior congressional approval in the form of Resolutions separately approved by a majority of the House of Reepresentatives and Senate shall be of no force and effect.

rows.abstract: Any person or entity who intends to import, possess or sell any of the chemicals used as ingredients in the manufacture of explosives shall file an application with the chief of Philippine National Police (PNP), stating the purpose for which the license and/or permit is sought and such inforamtion as may be required by the Chief of the PNP.> Any violation of the provisions of this Act shall be punished with imprisonment of not less than one (1) year but not more than five (5) years or a fine ofnot less than P10,000.00 pesos but not more than P100,000.00, or both, at the discretion of the court.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A SYSTEM OF REWARD AND OTHER INCENTIVES FOR PERSONS WHO COULD HELP IDENTIFY, LOCATE, PROVIDE INFORMATION, TESTIFY AND PROSECUTE VIOLATORS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3019, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-GRAFT AND CORRUPT PRACTICES ACT, AND OTHER CRIMINAL OFFENSES COMMITTED BY REASON OF THE FUNCTION OF PUBLIC OFFICE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3019
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Republic Act No. 3019 by providing a reward mechanism for informants of crimes committed by reason of public office. This reward mechanism provides incentives such as cash rewards, protection, security and other benefits forordinary citizens to participate in the government's fight against graft and corruption. It also grants not only the participants of the crime discharged as state witnesses, but also the most guilty one, the opportunity to redeem themselves by cooperating with the Office of the Ombudsman.

rows.abstract: "Tax Amnesty Law of 2002." This Act covers Income, Gift, Estate, Value Added Tax, Percentage and Excise taxes provided for under the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC), as amended, from Janury 1, 1993 to December 31, 2002. > Any taxpayer may avail of the tax amnesty provided in this Act except those with pending cases before any tribunal or any quasi-judicial body involving violations of the NIRC and/or covering ill-gotten or unexplained wealth and those already under investigation by concerned government bodies on or before December 31, 2002. Taxpayer who avails of this amnesty shall be exempt from any liability for the particular tax and period applied for.

rows.abstract: Section 109 of Republic Act No. 8435, otherwise known as the 'Agriculture and Fisheries Modernization Act (AFMA) of 1997,' is hereby amended by including all INDIVIDUALS, COOPERATIVES AND OTHER enterprises in the exemption of the payment of tariff and duties for the importation of all types of agriculture and fisheries inputs, equipment and machinery. > The AFMA provides for the exemption of all enterprises engaged in agriculture and fisheries, duty certified by the Department in consultation with the Department of Finance and the Board of Investment, from the payment of tariff and duties for the importation of all types of agriculture and fisheries inputs, equipment and machinery but only on the condition that the imported agricultural suupplies shall be used exclusively by the importing enterprise. rows.author: C095
rows.title_full: ACT PROVIDING FOR A SCHOOL NUTRITION PROGRAM
rows.abstract: "Child Nutrition Act of the Philippines." This bill aims to safeguard the health and well-being of the nation's children, encourage the domestic consumption of agricultural and other foods in order to meet more effectively the nutritional needs of our children. It seeks to established a School Nutrition Program who shall initiate, maintain and expand a system of distribution of milk and fortified snack foods to public elementary school entrants for a minimum of 120 feeding days, 5 times a week;and vitamin supplements for a period and in such dosages as may be determined by the Department of Health. > Incentives shall be given to local dairy cooperatives, private agricultural companies and other institutions donating food, milk, juices, viitamin supplements or other similar products provided that the donation is duly approved by the Secretary of Education, in case of vitamin products, and the Secretary of Health, in case of vitamin products.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2003-02-04

rows.author: C095
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FIVE (5)-YEAR EMERGENCY SCHOOLBUILDING PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "School Building Act of 2002." This bill mandates the Department of Education (DepEd) to undertake the following: (1) Fifteen thousand (15,000) additional classrooms every year, for a period of five (5) years, to address the classroom backlog in various parts of the country; (2) One elementary school in every barangay which does not have a public elementary school at the time of the passage of this Act; and (3) One high school in every town which does not have a public high school at the time of passage of this Act.> An amount of Fifteen Billion Pesos (P15,000,000,00 0) shall be set aside for the Emergency School Building Fund. It shall be used for school building and classroom construction, repair and rehabilitation for a period of five ((5) years as mandated in this Act.

rows.abstract: "Child Soldier's Act of 2002." This bill defines "child soldiers" as children who are direct or indirect participants to armed hostilities either as combatants, spies, guards, guides, lookouts, porters, garden workers, messengers or similar capacities. > Child soldiers who are rescued or surrendered shall be turned over, within twenty-four hours, to the nearest Field Office of the Deaprtment of Social Welfare and Development for protective custody and case evaluation. Immediate treatment shallalso be provided to the children wounded or suffering from any illness. This Act prohibits tactical interrogation by military and police authorities to such children unless permitted in writing by the Regional Director of the DSWD execising custody oover them. > Children who are already undergoing psychological/p sychiatric rehabilitation shall also be admitted into a scholarship program to resume their studies. rows.author: C020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR BLOCK VOTING IN THE ELECTIONS FOR PRESIDENT, VICE-PRESIDENT, GOVERNOR, VICE-GOVERNOR, MAYOR AND VICE-MAYOR
rows.abstract: This bill provides that the vote for the President shall be considered a vote for the Vice-President. Likewise, the vote for the Governor and Mayor shall also be considered a vote for the Vice-Governor and Vice-Mayor, respectively, PROVIDED, that both candidates shall be running under the same political party or aggrupation. > This proposed measure aims to achieve harmonious relationships which in turn will result in the achievement of a more unified leadership and devotion to solving the problems of the administration.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2003-02-11
